USA Today from Andrews McMeel's uclick data feed (code usaon). Named by the feed: usaonYYMMDD-data.xml. The feed carries no circles or shading.
Universal Sunday from Andrews McMeel's uclick data feed (code usun), the syndicate's own XML. Named by the feed: usunYYMMDD-data.xml.

Newsday's syndicate (Creators) set; the id encodes the date (Creators_WEB_YYYYMMDD).

Ids are the constructor's initials plus the date and a time (XXvox_YYYYMMDD_HHMM), so the id for a date is looked up on the date picker.
The 10x10 runs weekdays. The picker lists several puzzles under one date, so the id comes from the day's article page, which embeds the player.
Weekly, on Fridays (now and then a day late, which this calendar misses); ids are random hex, looked up on the date picker.

Defector's weekly crossword, on Mondays. Ids are random hex, looked up on the date picker. The payload names no editor. A bare year or "(c)" in the copyright line is written "© year", and "(Themeless)" is dropped from titles.

The daily is posted at 10 pm Eastern the evening before (6 pm on weekends). The Times rewrites clues after the day, hence the re-fetches. The feed has served complete puzzles without a session cookie since 2026-10; NYT_S, if set, is sent as the NYT-S cookie.
The Mini, posted the evening before like the daily.
The Midi, a 9x9 to 10x9 grid, posted the evening before like the daily.
The daily crossword runs Monday to Wednesday; year-end issue crosswords live under /magazine/ and are not fetched by date.
The Mini runs Thursday and Friday. The payload's date is the day it was made, not the day it ran; the file is named by the day it ran.
The Post's Sunday crossword from its games service, the JSON its player loads. The service answers an empty body for a Sunday it has no puzzle for.

The Arkadium Mini Crossword, from the feed behind Arkadium's player: Crossword Compiler XML, named by the feed (puzzle_mini_YYMMDD.xml). The feed holds a file for every date well into the next year. New puzzles ran 2018-12 to 2021 and once in 2024; every file since is a rerun of an earlier date, served under its own date. The feed's titles are the game's name or a batch number, so the title is the date.

The 2 Minute Mini, a 5x5 Arkadium publishes: the Across Lite file the feed behind its player serves, named by the feed (puzzle_YYMMDD.puz). The feed holds a file for every date well into the next year and has rerun earlier puzzles since 2024-01-30, each served under its own date. The feed's titles are numbers that don't identify a puzzle, so the title is the date. Some files have wrong .puz checksums.

The blog's crossword, posted every Monday (Themeless Monday) and Thursday. The day's post links the .puz (and a PDF, not fetched) under /files/, named by puzzle number and title (NNNNTitle.puz). The number param reads the puzzle number from that name; the date is the post's.

The Daily Princetonian's full-size crossword, from the API behind the paper's own crossword site. It has no fixed day: about one a week in term, none over breaks and exams, so every day is asked for and most are misses. The data has no grid; it is drawn from the clues' answers and positions.
The Daily Princetonian's mini, as for prnc. It runs in bursts of a few weekdays with long gaps, so every day is asked for and most are misses.
